unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-PREP YEAR-LEVEL: A2 - THEME 4: FAMILY LIFE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will write and design a comprehensive project on ''family members, routines of family members, hobbies of family members, relationships in the family'' exploring the roles, routines, hobbies, and relationships within a family. They will describe the daily routines and hobbies of family members, highlighting the roles each person plays in maintaining relationships, supporting each other’s interests, and balancing work and leisure. The project will also examine how family members interact with relatives, how they support one another’s activities, and the importance of maintaining healthy relationships within the family structure. As part of the project, students will write scripts for each family role, showcasing how family members contribute to family life, share hobbies, and engage in routines. These scripts will creatively illustrate how family members support and connect with one another in their day-to-day lives. The students will reflect on the relationships that tie the family together, emphasizing the significance of communication, shared activities, and mutual support in building and maintaining strong family bonds. The assignment will be evaluated using rubrics. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''family life with its components such as family members, routines of family members, hobbies of family members, relationships in the family'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what family members, routines of family members, hobbies of family members, relationships in the family mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''family life'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''a relationship, to communicate, divorced and so on'' and also some structures such as ''Ali is taller than Ahmet. Ali is the tallest in the class. My brother goes to school at 8 o’clock.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.

bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To understand, identify, and use target vocabulary about family members, their jobs, routines, and hobbies in English through a listening activity. Activity 1: Listening for Family Roles and Activities The teacher explains to the class that they will do a listening activity about family roles, routines, and hobbies. During the first listening, students focus on understanding the main ideas (e.g., ''My sister likes painting in her free time, while my brother enjoys cycling''). After the first listening, the teacher provides each student with a worksheet containing visuals (e.g., a person painting, someone cycling, a person working at a desk). The visuals have no text. During the second listening, students write down the activities or routines they hear under the appropriate visual (e.g., ''painting'' under a person with a paintbrush). During the third listening, students review and correct their answers. Afterwards, students share their answers with the class. The teacher provides constructive feedback by praising correct matches (e.g., ''Great job, you correctly identified the hobbies!''). Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity Objective: To understand and talk about family members’ jobs, routines, and hobbies in English through reading activity by using target vocabulary. Activity 2: Family Member Puzzle Reading Students are divided into groups of four, with each student receiving a different part of a short reading passage about a fictional family (e.g., ''Mr. Smith works as a mechanic and enjoys fixing things at home. Mrs. Smith is a teacher who loves gardening in her free time. Emily, their daughter, is an artistic student who loves painting, while Jake, her brother, prefers playing football''. Each section includes questions such as ''What is Mr. Smith’s job?'', ''What does Jake enjoy doing?''. Students answer their questions, then ask each other about the missing information to complete the full family profile. Afterward, groups present their findings to the class, and the teacher provides feedback on grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To help students use target vocabulary related to family members and their routines while improving writing and speaking skills. Objective: To identify and talk about family members and their routines in English by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Choose the Correct Word The teacher provides a worksheet with pictures depicting family-related activities and members (e.g., siblings playing, grandparents gardening, a mother cooking) along with a word bank containing words like siblings, grandparents, mother, gardening, cooking, relaxing, drawing, and painting. Students examine the pictures and write the correct word under each image (e.g., for grandparents gardening, write ''grandparents gardening''). Once completed, the teacher points to each picture, asks, ''Who is this, and what are they doing?'' and encourages students to respond in full sentences, such as ''These are grandparents, and they are gardening'', while providing feedback on pronunciation and accuracy. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To help students describe and compare family members’ routines and hobbies using visuals and target vocabulary. Activity 2: Fill in the Blanks (Interactive with Visuals) The teacher presents an interactive activity with pictures of family members performing tasks (e.g., cooking, gardening, teaching). Each question shows a visual with an incomplete sentence and multiplechoice options for students to select the correct word. For example, a picture of a mother cooking is paired with the sentence, ''My mother is a cook. She ____________ delicious meals every day'', with choices like ''cooks, teaches, and grows''. For comparisons, side-by-side visuals, such as a father farming and a mother teaching, are provided with sentences like ''My father ____________ vegetables, but my mother ____________ lessons'', followed by a comparative statement: ''My father’s job is ____________, but my mother’s job is ____________,'',with options like ''harder/easier'' or ''more rewarding/less tiring''. After completing the activity, students share their answers orally, forming sentences such as ''My father’s job is harder than my mother’s job, but my mother’s job is more rewarding than my father’s job''. The teacher provides feedback on grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation, reinforcing the use of comparative adjectives and target verbs. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
